name: NASA
description: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration is the United States government agency responsible for aeronautics and space exploration. NASA leads groundbreaking missions including the Artemis lunar program, Mars exploration, and the James Webb Space Telescope.
notableAchievements: Apollo Moon landings; Space Shuttle program; International Space Station; Mars rovers; Artemis program
activeProducts: Artemis; SLS; Orion; Commercial Crew Program

name: SpaceX
description: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. is the world's leading commercial launch provider, revolutionizing space access through reusable rocket technology. SpaceX operates Starlink, the largest satellite constellation, and is developing Starship for interplanetary travel.
notableAchievements: First private company to ISS; Reusable orbital rockets; Crew Dragon certification; Starlink global coverage
activeProducts: Falcon 9; Falcon Heavy; Starship; Dragon; Starlink

name: Blue Origin
description: Blue Origin is developing reusable launch vehicles and space systems with the vision of enabling a future where millions of people live and work in space. The company operates New Shepard suborbital flights and is developing the New Glenn orbital rocket.
notableAchievements: New Shepard reusability; BE-4 engine development; Blue Moon lunar lander selection
activeProducts: New Shepard; New Glenn; BE-4 Engine; Blue Moon

name: United Launch Alliance
description: United Launch Alliance is a joint venture between Boeing and Lockheed Martin, providing reliable launch services for U.S. government and commercial customers. ULA maintains a 100% mission success rate with Atlas V and is transitioning to Vulcan Centaur.
notableAchievements: 100% mission success rate; 150+ successful launches; Vulcan Centaur first flight 2024

name: Rocket Lab
description: Rocket Lab is an end-to-end space company delivering reliable launch services, satellite manufacturing, spacecraft components, and on-orbit management. Operating from sites in New Zealand and Virginia, they've launched over 180 satellites.
notableAchievements: First private orbital launch from Southern Hemisphere; Electron rocket reusability; Neutron development
activeProducts: Electron; Neutron; Photon spacecraft; Pioneer spacecraft bus

name: Firefly Aerospace
description: Firefly Aerospace provides launch vehicles for small-to-medium payloads and developed the Blue Ghost lunar lander. Blue Ghost Mission 1 successfully landed on the Moon in January 2025, making Firefly one of the first commercial companies to achieve a lunar landing. Awarded $177M NASA follow-on CLPS contract. Medium Launch Vehicle (MLV) in development for 2026 debut.
notableAchievements: Blue Ghost lunar landing (Jan 2025); Alpha orbital success; NASA CLPS contract; $177M NASA follow-on; Blue Ghost 2 mission confirmed Q2 2026
activeProducts: Alpha; MLV (in development); Blue Ghost lander

name: Relativity Space
description: Relativity Space is pioneering 3D-printed rockets, using the world's largest metal 3D printers to manufacture launch vehicles. Their Terran R rocket aims to provide medium-lift capabilities with rapid manufacturing turnaround.
notableAchievements: World's first 3D-printed rocket to reach space; Stargate 3D printer technology

name: ABL Space Systems
description: ABL Space Systems is developing low-cost, rapidly deployable launch services with their RS1 rocket. The company focuses on streamlined operations from containerized ground systems.
notableAchievements: Amazon Project Kuiper contract

name: Astra Space
description: Astra went private in July 2024 after founders acquired all shares at $0.50/share. The company halted rocket launches and pivoted to spacecraft propulsion systems (electric engines). Now profitable with ~125 employees, focused on satellite engines and a new launch vehicle in development.
notableAchievements: Went private (July 2024); Pivoted to propulsion systems; Returned to profitability

name: Virgin Galactic
description: Virgin Galactic paused all commercial spaceflight operations in June 2024 and retired VSS Unity to focus on developing next-generation Delta-class vehicles. Test flights are targeted for Q3 2026, with commercial service resumption expected in 2027.
notableAchievements: First commercial spaceflight with passengers; Unity spaceship flights; Delta-class in development

name: Intuitive Machines
description: Intuitive Machines is a space exploration company providing lunar access services. Their Nova-C lander became the first commercial spacecraft to successfully land on the Moon in 2024.
notableAchievements: First US Moon landing since Apollo (2024); NASA CLPS contract holder

name: Astrobotic
description: Astrobotic is a lunar logistics company providing delivery services to the Moon. The company develops the Peregrine and Griffin landers for NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services program.
notableAchievements: NASA VIPER rover contract; Multiple CLPS missions

name: Planet Labs
description: Planet Labs operates the largest constellation of Earth observation satellites, providing daily global imagery and analytics. Their fleet of Dove and SuperDove satellites capture the entire Earth's landmass daily.
notableAchievements: Largest Earth imaging constellation; Daily global coverage
activeProducts: Dove satellites; SuperDove satellites; SkySat; Planet Analytics

name: Maxar Technologies
description: Maxar Technologies is a space technology company specializing in Earth intelligence, geospatial data, and satellite manufacturing. They provide high-resolution satellite imagery and geospatial solutions.
notableAchievements: WorldView satellite constellation; Power and Propulsion Element for Lunar Gateway

name: Axiom Space
description: Axiom Space is building the world's first commercial space station, with Axiom Station Module 1 on track for ISS attachment. The company has conducted four private astronaut missions to the ISS and delivered NASA's next-generation Artemis spacesuits.
notableAchievements: Four private astronaut missions to ISS; NASA Artemis spacesuit contract; Axiom Station Module 1 in production; NASA commercial destination award
activeProducts: Axiom Station modules; AxEMU spacesuit; Private astronaut missions

name: Sierra Space
description: Sierra Space is developing the Dream Chaser spaceplane and LIFE habitat for the Orbital Reef commercial space station. The company aims to create a thriving space economy.
notableAchievements: Dream Chaser spaceplane development; Orbital Reef partnership with Blue Origin

name: Northrop Grumman Space
description: Northrop Grumman's Space Systems sector provides launch vehicles, satellites, and space logistics. They operate Cygnus cargo spacecraft and developed the MEV satellite servicing vehicles.
notableAchievements: MEV-1 first commercial satellite servicing; Antares/Cygnus ISS resupply
activeProducts: Antares; Cygnus; MEV; National security satellites

name: Lockheed Martin Space
description: Lockheed Martin Space designs, develops, and operates advanced space systems including satellites, spacecraft, and exploration vehicles. They are building the Orion spacecraft for Artemis.
notableAchievements: Orion spacecraft; Mars missions; GPS satellites
activeProducts: Orion; GPS III satellites; Space-based missiles defense

name: Boeing Space & Launch
description: Boeing Space & Launch develops spacecraft, satellites, and launch systems. The company operates the CST-100 Starliner crew vehicle and contributed to the International Space Station.
notableAchievements: ISS construction; Starliner crewed flight; SLS core stage
activeProducts: Starliner; SLS core stage; X-37B; Satellites

name: Terran Orbital (Lockheed Martin)
description: Terran Orbital was acquired by Lockheed Martin in October 2024 for ~$450M enterprise value. Now operating as 'Terran Orbital, a Lockheed Martin Company,' it continues as a merchant supplier of small satellites for military, civil, and commercial customers under Lockheed Martin's Space division.
notableAchievements: Acquired by Lockheed Martin (Oct 2024); Rivada constellation contract; SDA Tranche satellites

name: Viasat
description: Viasat is a global communications company providing high-speed satellite broadband services and secure networking systems. Their ViaSat-3 constellation provides ultra-high capacity connectivity.
notableAchievements: ViaSat-3 launch; Inmarsat acquisition; Global coverage

name: Iridium Communications
description: Iridium operates the world's only truly global satellite communications network, providing voice and data connectivity anywhere on Earth. The Iridium NEXT constellation offers enhanced capabilities including Iridium Certus broadband.
notableAchievements: Global satellite network; Iridium NEXT constellation; Direct-to-device partnerships
activeProducts: Iridium NEXT; Iridium Certus; IoT services

name: Impulse Space
description: Impulse Space develops in-space transportation vehicles to deliver satellites to precise orbits. Founded by former SpaceX propulsion director Tom Mueller, the company launched its upgraded Mira vehicle on LEO Express-3 and debuted the Helios kick stage in early 2026. Impulse has partnered with Anduril for an RPO (rendezvous & proximity operations) demo mission.
notableAchievements: Mira OTV operational; Helios kick stage debut (2026); LEO Express-3 mission success; Anduril RPO demo partnership; Series B funding secured

name: Varda Space Industries
description: Varda Space Industries manufactures products in microgravity and returns them to Earth. The company focuses on pharmaceutical compounds and advanced materials that benefit from space production.
notableAchievements: First commercial in-space manufacturing mission; Successful capsule return 2024

name: Anduril Industries
description: Anduril Industries is a defense technology company building autonomous systems and AI-powered platforms for national security. In the space domain, Anduril is positioning for the Golden Dome missile defense architecture with satellite-based interceptor and sensor systems, partnering with Apex Space for satellite bus supply.
notableAchievements: $14B+ valuation; Golden Dome positioning; Apex Space partnership for satellite buses; Lattice AI platform

name: Apex Space
description: Apex Space is the leading mass-manufacturer of configurable satellite buses for defense and commercial constellations. Its three platforms — Aries, Nova, and Comet — carry 100 to 5,000 kg of payload. The company reached unicorn status in 2025 with $500M+ raised, and its factory produces 200+ satellite buses per year.
notableAchievements: $1B+ valuation in 3 years; Project Shadow orbital interceptor demo; 200+ satellite bus annual production capacity; Anduril strategic partnership
activeProducts: Aries Bus; Nova Bus; Comet Bus; Orbital Magazine

name: K2 Space
description: K2 Space builds mega-class satellites that deliver 10x the power of traditional satellite buses at a fraction of the cost. With $441M+ raised at a $3B valuation, the company has $500M in signed contracts and a 180,000 sq ft factory producing up to 100 satellites per year.
notableAchievements: $3B valuation; $500M in signed contracts; GRAVITAS satellite launching March 2026; SES partnership for MEO constellation

name: Portal Space Systems
description: Portal Space Systems develops the Afterburner, a solar thermal propulsion system that uses concentrated sunlight to superheat propellant, delivering higher specific impulse than chemical thrusters at a fraction of the cost. The technology enables sustained, responsive spacecraft maneuvering for defense and commercial constellations.
notableAchievements: Solar thermal propulsion development; Flagged in Payload Space Golden Dome review

name: Quantum Space
description: Quantum Space provides cislunar situational awareness and relay infrastructure, positioning communications and navigation nodes beyond GEO to support lunar missions and defense operations. Backed by Draper Laboratory, the company's Eos spacecraft program has drawn U.S. Space Force interest.
notableAchievements: Draper Laboratory backing; Eos spacecraft program; U.S. Space Force interest; Cislunar relay architecture

name: True Anomaly
description: True Anomaly builds autonomous orbital vehicles and space domain awareness software. Its Jackal vehicle can maneuver, track, and operate against threats on orbit, while its Mosaic software provides AI-driven space domain awareness for defense applications.
notableAchievements: $389M raised Series C; $30M VICTUS HAZE Space Force contract; Classified OTA for boost-phase interceptor prototypes; Jackal autonomous orbital vehicle

name: Voyager Technologies
description: Voyager Technologies (NYSE: VOYG) is the only publicly traded pure-play in the tier-2 defense space supply chain. The company acquired ExoTerra Resource for electric propulsion systems and holds a patent for producing ultra-pure optical crystals in microgravity. Key programs include Starlab commercial space station.
notableAchievements: IPO June 2025 (NYSE: VOYG); ExoTerra acquisition for electric propulsion; Microgravity optical crystal patent; NASA $217.5M Starlab grant

name: European Space Agency
description: The European Space Agency is an intergovernmental organization of 22 member states dedicated to space exploration. ESA coordinates European space activities and develops rockets, spacecraft, and space infrastructure.
notableAchievements: Rosetta comet mission; Galileo navigation; Copernicus Earth observation; Ariane program

name: Arianespace
description: Arianespace is the world's first commercial launch services company, operating from Europe's Spaceport in French Guiana. The company provides launch services using Ariane 6 and Vega rockets.
notableAchievements: 400+ satellite launches; Ariane 5 success record; Ariane 6 inaugural flight 2024

name: ArianeGroup
description: ArianeGroup is a joint venture between Airbus and Safran, developing and manufacturing the Ariane 6 launcher. The company leads European access to space with propulsion and launch vehicle expertise.
notableAchievements: Ariane 6 development; Prometheus reusable engine
activeProducts: Ariane 6; Prometheus engine; Vinci upper stage

name: Isar Aerospace
description: Isar Aerospace is developing Spectrum, a new European launch vehicle designed for small and medium payloads. The company aims to provide flexible, cost-effective access to space from European soil.
notableAchievements: ESA launch services contract; Andøya launch site agreement

name: Rocket Factory Augsburg
description: Rocket Factory Augsburg is developing RFA ONE, a German-designed orbital rocket. The company aims to provide European launch services at competitive prices with rapid manufacturing.
notableAchievements: Staged combustion engine development; SaxaVord launch agreement

name: OHB SE
description: OHB SE is one of Europe's leading space and technology companies, specializing in satellites, aerospace structures, and data analytics. The company has delivered numerous Galileo satellites.
notableAchievements: Galileo satellites; EnMAP hyperspectral mission; PLATO telescope
activeProducts: Galileo satellites; Earth observation satellites; Space systems

name: PLD Space
description: PLD Space is developing reusable launch vehicles to provide affordable small satellite launch services from Europe. The company successfully launched Miura 1 in 2023.
notableAchievements: First Spanish rocket to reach space (Miura 1); Reusable technology development

name: Orbex
description: Orbex is developing Prime, an environmentally sustainable orbital rocket designed for small satellite launches. The company operates from Sutherland Spaceport in Scotland.
notableAchievements: Bio-propane fueled rocket; 3D-printed rocket engine; Sutherland Spaceport

name: Skyrora
description: Skyrora is a UK launch company developing Skyrora XL, an orbital rocket for small satellite deployment. The company uses innovative manufacturing and eco-friendly propellants.
notableAchievements: Skylark L suborbital flights; Ecosene sustainable fuel

name: SaxaVord UK Spaceport
description: SaxaVord is the UK's first vertical launch spaceport, located on Unst in the Shetland Islands. The site provides launch services for small satellite operators seeking polar and sun-synchronous orbits.
notableAchievements: First licensed UK spaceport; Multiple launch provider agreements

name: Telespazio
description: Telespazio is a joint venture between Leonardo and Thales, providing satellite operations, Earth observation services, and space infrastructure management. The company operates one of Europe's largest ground station networks.
notableAchievements: Fucino Space Centre; Galileo operations; Copernicus ground segment

name: Thales Alenia Space
description: Thales Alenia Space is a joint venture between Thales and Leonardo. In October 2025, the parent companies signed an MoU with Airbus to merge European space divisions (excluding launch) into a consolidated entity, expected operational by 2027. Specializes in telecom, Earth observation, space exploration, and orbital infrastructure.
notableAchievements: ISS modules; Galileo satellites; Hera asteroid mission
activeProducts: Telecommunications satellites; Navigation payloads; Orbital modules

name: Airbus Defence and Space
description: Airbus Defence and Space is Europe's largest space company, designing and manufacturing satellites, orbital systems, and launcher components. In October 2025, Airbus signed an MoU with Leonardo and Thales to merge their space divisions (excluding launch) into a joint European space entity, expected operational by 2027.
notableAchievements: OneSat platform; Eurostar NEO; Bartolomeo ISS platform
activeProducts: Telecommunications satellites; Earth observation systems; Ariane 6 components

name: China National Space Administration
description: CNSA is the national space agency of China responsible for planning and development of space activities. The agency oversees China's ambitious lunar, Mars, and space station programs.
notableAchievements: Tiangong space station; Chang'e lunar missions; Tianwen Mars mission

name: China Aerospace Science & Technology
description: CASC is China's main contractor for space activities, developing the Long March rocket family and operating China's human spaceflight and deep space exploration programs.
notableAchievements: Long March rocket family; Shenzhou crewed flights; BeiDou constellation
activeProducts: Long March 5; Long March 7; Shenzhou; Tianzhou

name: LandSpace
description: LandSpace is one of China's leading commercial launch companies, developing the Zhuque rocket series. Zhuque-2 became the world's first methane-fueled rocket to reach orbit.
notableAchievements: First methane rocket to orbit (Zhuque-2); Reusable rocket development

name: iSpace (China)
description: Beijing Interstellar Glory Space Technology (iSpace) is a Chinese commercial launch company developing the Hyperbola rocket series for small satellite launches.
notableAchievements: First Chinese private company to reach orbit

name: Galactic Energy
description: Galactic Energy develops commercial launch vehicles including the Ceres-1 solid rocket and Pallas-1 reusable liquid rocket. The company has achieved multiple successful orbital launches.
notableAchievements: Multiple Ceres-1 orbital successes; Pallas-1 development

name: Deep Blue Aerospace
description: Deep Blue Aerospace is developing reusable rocket technology with the Nebula-1 rocket. The company has demonstrated successful vertical takeoff and landing tests.
notableAchievements: VTVL rocket testing; Reusable first stage development

name: Indian Space Research Organisation
description: ISRO is India's national space agency, known for cost-effective space missions. ISRO has achieved significant milestones including Mars Orbiter Mission and Chandrayaan lunar program.
notableAchievements: Mars Orbiter Mission; Chandrayaan-3 lunar landing; Gaganyaan development

name: Agnikul Cosmos
description: Agnikul Cosmos is developing 3D-printed rocket engines and the Agnibaan launch vehicle for small satellite deployment. The company achieved the world's first 3D-printed single-piece rocket engine.
notableAchievements: World's first single-piece 3D-printed rocket engine; ISRO technical partnership

name: Skyroot Aerospace
description: Skyroot Aerospace became India's first private company to launch a rocket to space with Vikram-S in 2022. The company is developing the Vikram rocket family for small satellite launches.
notableAchievements: First private Indian space launch (Vikram-S); Dhawan engine development

name: Pixxel
description: Pixxel is building the world's highest resolution hyperspectral satellite constellation to monitor environmental and agricultural changes from space.
notableAchievements: Shakuntala hyperspectral satellite; SpaceX launch partnership

name: Bellatrix Aerospace
description: Bellatrix Aerospace develops advanced propulsion systems including green propellant thrusters and electric propulsion for satellites and orbital transfer vehicles.
notableAchievements: India's first private in-space propulsion system; Green propulsion development
activeProducts: Arka OTV; Hall thrusters; Green monopropellant

name: Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency
description: JAXA is Japan's national aerospace agency conducting space, aviation, and research activities. JAXA operates the H3 rocket and leads missions including asteroid sample return and lunar exploration.
notableAchievements: Hayabusa asteroid sample return; H-IIA/H3 rockets; ISS Kibo module

name: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries
description: MHI is Japan's primary launch vehicle manufacturer, developing and operating the H-IIA and H3 rockets. The company also manufactures satellites and space station components.
notableAchievements: 50+ H-IIA launches; H3 development; ISS supply missions

name: ispace
description: ispace is a lunar exploration company developing HAKUTO-R lunar landers and rovers. The company aims to extend human presence beyond Earth through lunar infrastructure development.
notableAchievements: HAKUTO-R Mission 1; Multiple NASA CLPS payload contracts

name: Synspective
description: Synspective develops and operates small SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) satellites for all-weather, day-and-night Earth observation. The company provides geospatial data solutions.
notableAchievements: StriX SAR constellation; Land Displacement Monitoring service
activeProducts: StriX satellites; Land Displacement Monitoring; Flood Damage Assessment

name: Astroscale
description: Astroscale is the world leader in orbital debris removal and satellite servicing. The company develops technologies for sustainable space operations and end-of-life satellite services.
notableAchievements: ELSA-d debris removal demonstration; JAXA ADRAS-J mission

name: Roscosmos
description: Roscosmos is the Russian state space corporation responsible for Russia's space program. The agency operates human spaceflight, launch services, and maintains the Russian ISS segment.
notableAchievements: Mir space station; Soyuz reliability record; ISS partnership

name: RSC Energia
description: RSC Energia is Russia's primary human spaceflight contractor, manufacturing Soyuz and Progress spacecraft. The company traces its heritage to Sergei Korolev's design bureau.
notableAchievements: Soyuz spacecraft; Mir modules; ISS Russian segment
activeProducts: Soyuz MS; Progress MS; Nauka module

name: Israel Space Agency
description: The Israel Space Agency coordinates Israel's space program and research activities. ISA oversees satellite development and international space partnerships.
notableAchievements: Beresheet lunar attempt; EROS satellite series; Shavit launches

name: Israel Aerospace Industries
description: IAI Space is Israel's main aerospace and defense company, developing satellites, launch vehicles, and space systems. IAI built Israel's reconnaissance satellite constellation.
notableAchievements: Shavit launcher; AMOS satellite series; OFEQ reconnaissance satellites

name: Canadian Space Agency
description: The Canadian Space Agency coordinates Canada's space activities and partnerships, including significant contributions to the ISS through the Canadarm2 robotic system.
notableAchievements: Canadarm; Canadarm2; Dextre; RADARSAT constellation
activeProducts: Lunar Gateway contributions; RADARSAT; Astronaut program

name: MDA Space
description: MDA Space is a leading space technology company known for developing Canadarm, Canadarm2, and advanced satellite systems. The company specializes in robotics, satellite systems, and geointelligence.
notableAchievements: Canadarm legacy; Lunar Gateway Canadarm3 contract; RADARSAT Constellation

name: Telesat
description: Telesat operates one of the world's largest satellite fleets and is developing Telesat Lightspeed, a LEO constellation for global enterprise-grade connectivity.
notableAchievements: 50+ years in satellite communications; Telesat Lightspeed development

name: Korea Aerospace Research Institute
description: KARI is South Korea's aerospace research institute responsible for developing the KSLV rockets. KARI achieved the successful Nuri rocket launches, establishing Korea's independent space access.
notableAchievements: KSLV-II Nuri successful launches; Korea Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter

name: Hanwha Aerospace
description: Hanwha Aerospace is a leading Korean aerospace and defense company developing satellite systems and rocket propulsion. The company is investing heavily in space capabilities.
notableAchievements: Korean satellite production; Satrec Initiative acquisition
activeProducts: Satellite buses; Propulsion systems; Space ventures

name: UAE Space Agency
description: The UAE Space Agency regulates and supports the UAE's rapidly growing space sector. The agency has overseen ambitious missions including the Hope Mars Orbiter.
notableAchievements: Hope Mars Orbiter (first Arab interplanetary mission); Rashid lunar rover
activeProducts: National space strategy; Space research programs

name: Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Centre
description: MBRSC is Dubai's space center responsible for developing satellites and space missions. The center built the Hope Mars orbiter and the Rashid lunar rover.
notableAchievements: Hope (Al-Amal) Mars mission; Rashid lunar rovers; DubaiSat series

name: Australian Space Agency
description: The Australian Space Agency coordinates national space activities and works to grow Australia's space industry. The agency focuses on Earth observation, communications, and space situational awareness.
notableAchievements: Artemis Accords signatory; Moon to Mars initiative

name: Gilmour Space Technologies
description: Gilmour Space Technologies is developing the Eris rocket for small satellite launches from Australia. The company aims to provide sovereign launch capability for the Indo-Pacific region.
notableAchievements: Hybrid rocket engine development; Bowen launch site development

name: Luxembourg Space Agency
description: The Luxembourg Space Agency promotes space activities and coordinates the country's SpaceResources.lu initiative for space resources utilization. Luxembourg is a hub for space mining companies.
notableAchievements: First European space resources law; SpaceResources.lu initiative

name: SES
description: SES is one of the world's leading satellite operators, providing global content connectivity solutions through a fleet of GEO and MEO satellites including the O3b mPOWER constellation.
notableAchievements: O3b MEO constellation; Global video distribution; Government solutions

name: Turkish Space Agency
description: The Turkish Space Agency coordinates Turkey's space activities and implements the National Space Program, including lunar mission plans and domestic satellite development.
notableAchievements: National Space Program 2021; First Turkish astronaut mission planning

name: Roketsan
description: Roketsan is Turkey's leading rocket and missile manufacturer, developing space launch capabilities. The company is working on solid rocket motors and small launch vehicles.
notableAchievements: Solid rocket motor development; Space launch vehicle program

name: Brazilian Space Agency
description: The Brazilian Space Agency coordinates Brazil's space activities, including the Alcântara Launch Center development and satellite programs with INPE.
notableAchievements: Alcântara Launch Center (optimal equatorial location); CBERS satellite partnership with China
activeProducts: VLS rocket development; Alcântara commercial launches

name: Italian Space Agency
description: ASI is the Italian national space agency coordinating Italy's significant space activities. Italy is a major contributor to European space programs and ISS modules.
notableAchievements: ISS modules (Columbus, Cupola); COSMO-SkyMed constellation; Vega rocket leadership
activeProducts: Space research; ISS contributions; Earth observation

name: Avio
description: Avio is an Italian aerospace company that develops and produces the Vega small launch vehicle for ESA. The company specializes in solid and liquid rocket propulsion systems.
notableAchievements: Vega launch vehicle; Vega-C development; Ariane boosters

name: CNES
description: CNES is the French national space agency and a major contributor to European space activities. CNES operates the Guiana Space Centre and leads numerous satellite and exploration programs.
notableAchievements: Guiana Space Centre; Ariane program leadership; Mars missions
activeProducts: Launch complex operations; Space research; Earth observation

name: Norwegian Space Agency
description: The Norwegian Space Agency coordinates Norway's space activities, focusing on Earth observation, satellite communications, and Arctic monitoring capabilities.
notableAchievements: Arctic satellite ground stations; ESA contributions; NorSat series

name: Andøya Space
description: Andøya Space operates sounding rocket and balloon launch facilities in northern Norway. The company is developing Andøya Spaceport for small satellite orbital launches.
notableAchievements: 1,200+ sounding rocket launches; Andøya Spaceport development
activeProducts: Sounding rockets; Andøya Spaceport; Satellite ground stations

name: UK Space Agency
description: The UK Space Agency is responsible for all strategic decisions on the UK civil space programme and represents the UK in ESA. The agency is developing UK launch capabilities.
notableAchievements: UK spaceport development; ESA contributions; OneWeb rescue

name: Surrey Satellite Technology
description: SSTL is a world leader in small satellite design and manufacture. The company has built over 70 satellites and pioneered low-cost, high-capability small satellite missions.
notableAchievements: 70+ satellites delivered; DMC constellation; Galileo IOV satellites
activeProducts: Earth observation satellites; Navigation payloads; Platforms

name: Office for Space Technology & Industry
description: OSTIn coordinates Singapore's space industry development and research activities. Singapore focuses on satellite technology, space robotics, and downstream applications.
notableAchievements: Singapore Space Technology Association support; Satellite hub development

name: Saudi Space Agency
description: The Saudi Space Agency is developing Saudi Arabia's space capabilities as part of Vision 2030. The agency is building domestic satellite capability and astronaut programs.
notableAchievements: First Saudi astronauts; Domestic satellite development programs

name: Spire Global
description: Spire Global operates a constellation of nanosatellites providing weather, maritime, and aviation tracking data. The company collects and analyzes data from space for various industries.
notableAchievements: 100+ satellite constellation; Global AIS coverage; Weather data services
activeProducts: Lemur nanosatellites; Maritime data; Weather analytics

name: BlackSky
description: BlackSky provides real-time geospatial intelligence through its constellation of high-resolution imaging satellites and AI-powered analytics platform.
notableAchievements: Real-time intelligence platform; Defense and commercial contracts

name: Capella Space (IonQ)
description: Capella Space operates a constellation of SAR satellites providing high-resolution radar imagery day or night, through any weather. Acquired by IonQ (NYSE: IONQ) in July 2025 to build a space-based quantum key distribution (QKD) network. Leadership team remains in place; satellite operations continue uninterrupted.
notableAchievements: Acquired by IonQ (July 2025); First US commercial SAR satellite; Sub-meter resolution SAR
activeProducts: Whitney satellites; SAR data services; QKD network (development)

name: Stoke Space
description: Stoke Space is developing a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Founded by former Blue Origin engineers, the company raised $860M in a Series D at ~$2B valuation. Its Nova rocket is in final pre-launch testing as of mid-2026, selected for NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1.
notableAchievements: Full-flow staged combustion engine; Reusable upper stage hover test; $860M Series D at ~$2B valuation; NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1 selection; Nova rocket in final testing (2026)

description: Phantom Space is developing affordable launch vehicles and satellite solutions. The company aims to democratize space access with low-cost rockets and satellite platforms.
notableAchievements: Daytona rocket development; Integrated space solutions

name: Vast

notableAchievements: NASA Commercial LEO Destination award; Multi-company partnership

name: EarthDaily Analytics
description: Observing verifying and predicting changes to the Earth's surface to help people understand and take action.

name: EchoStar
description: Providing satellite communication solutions and broadband services.
notableAchievements: Hughes Network Systems acquisition; Jupiter satellite fleet

name: EUMETSAT
description: Monitoring weather climate and environment to support people and industries worldwide.
notableAchievements: Meteosat program; Global weather monitoring

name: Exotrail
description: Designs develops and operates agile space mobility solutions for small satellites.
activeProducts: ExoMG thrusters; SpaceVan orbital transfer vehicle

name: GHGSat
description: Measuring emissions from space with high-resolution greenhouse gas monitoring.
notableAchievements: World's first commercial satellite for methane monitoring

name: GITAI USA
description: Developing robotic systems for building and maintaining satellites and space habitats.
notableAchievements: ISS robotics demonstration

name: ICEYE
description: Delivering persistent monitoring with SAR satellite technology for all-weather imaging.
notableAchievements: First commercial SAR satellite under 100kg

name: Inversion
description: Developing high cadence re-entry vehicles to enable easy return from space.

name: Jet Propulsion Laboratory
description: Space research and development center managed for NASA by the California Institute of Technology.
notableAchievements: Mars rovers; Voyager missions; Cassini-Huygens

name: Kepler Communications
description: Designing building launching and operating a network of LEO satellites to bring internet to outer space.

name: LeoLabs
description: Developing software to help commercial enterprises and agencies launch and track missions in LEO.
notableAchievements: Global radar network

name: Loft Orbital
description: Deploying space infrastructure as a service providing rapid reliable and simplified access to space.

name: Lunar Outpost
description: Enabling extended human presence in space with autonomous Lunar Rovers and sensor systems.
notableAchievements: MOXIE rover for NASA

name: Lynk Global
description: Lynk Global provides direct-to-phone satellite connectivity using nanosatellites. In October 2025, Lynk announced a merger with Omnispace for comprehensive D2D connectivity, with SES becoming a major strategic partner.
notableAchievements: First text from space to unmodified phone; Omnispace merger (Oct 2025); SES partnership
activeProducts: Lynk satellite constellation; D2D connectivity platform

name: Momentus
description: Momentus provides in-space transportation via its Vigoride orbital transfer vehicle. After near-bankruptcy in 2024 and restructuring, Momentus completed its Vigoride-7 mission in 2025. The company trades at micro-cap levels on Nasdaq and is focused on winning government and commercial OTV contracts to stabilize revenue.

name: Muon Space
description: Understanding predicting and modeling our changing planet through space-based sensor networks.

name: Mynaric
description: Revolutionizing laser communications for air space and mobile applications.

name: Open Cosmos
description: Providing simple and affordable satellite missions with end-to-end solutions.

name: Outpost
description: Pioneering multi-ton Earth return for the growing space economy and point-to-point delivery.

name: Redwire Space
description: Developing mission critical solutions for next generation space infrastructure.
notableAchievements: ISS solar arrays; In-space manufacturing

name: Satellogic
description: Satellogic delivers high-resolution satellite imagery via a LEO constellation. The company's 2024 10-K filing (March 2025) disclosed going concern doubt, citing cash constraints. Operations continue but financial outlook remains uncertain.

name: Slingshot Aerospace
description: Bringing together data from multiple sources to provide a full dynamic orbital picture.

name: Space Perspective
description: Offering a safe and accessible six-hour journey to the edge of space in a giant SpaceBalloon.

name: SpinLaunch
description: Developing a revolutionary kinetic launch system for affordable frequent access to space for small satellites.
notableAchievements: Successful suborbital test flights

name: Stratolaunch
description: Designing manufacturing and launching aerospace vehicles for space access and hypersonic flight.
notableAchievements: World's largest wingspan aircraft
activeProducts: Roc carrier aircraft; Talon-A hypersonic vehicle

name: The Aerospace Corporation
description: Providing technical expertise for space programs and national security missions.

name: Turion Space
description: Building spacecraft for national security and in-space servicing making space safer smarter and more sustainable.

name: Umbra
description: Developing space systems for observing the Earth in high resolution with SAR technology.

name: Ursa Major
description: Developing propulsion systems for space launch hypersonics and national security applications.
notableAchievements: Hadley engine production

name: Venus Aerospace
description: Developing high-speed hypersonic transportation for one-hour global travel.

name: Xona Space Systems
description: Developing a real-time positioning navigation and timing service for global navigation.

name: York Space Systems
description: Providing end-to-end mission solutions for next-gen space operations.
notableAchievements: S-CLASS platform

name: Zeno Power
description: Developing space-based nuclear power systems using nuclear waste for long-duration missions.

name: Starfish Space
description: Starfish Space develops satellite servicing vehicles for rendezvous, proximity operations, and docking (RPO&D). The company's Otter spacecraft demonstrated autonomous docking in orbit in 2024, making it one of the first commercial RPO successes.
notableAchievements: Otter RPO demo (2024); Autonomous satellite docking; DARPA NOM-4 contract

name: Scout Space
description: Scout Space builds space-based space domain awareness (SDA) sensors. Its Owl satellites observe other spacecraft from orbit, providing real-time custody tracking for defense and commercial customers.
notableAchievements: First commercial SDA satellite launched; U.S. Space Force contracts

name: Castelion
description: Castelion builds hypersonic vehicles and orbital platforms for defense applications. The company completed rapid manufacturing of its Hatchet vehicle and secured contracts for missile defense and prompt global strike architecture.
notableAchievements: Hatchet vehicle development; DoD defense contracts; Rapid manufacturing capability

name: Epsilon3
description: Epsilon3 provides an operating system for launch and spacecraft operations, digitizing test and launch procedures. Used by major launch providers and NASA programs to replace paper-based workflows with real-time collaboration tools.
notableAchievements: Used by NASA, SpaceX, Firefly, Relativity; Y Combinator graduate

name: Hermeus
description: Hermeus is developing Mach 5+ hypersonic aircraft, including the Quarterhorse autonomous testbed and the Halcyon passenger vehicle. The company has USAF contracts for hypersonic flight testing and completed its first engine test in 2024.
notableAchievements: Quarterhorse Mk 1 taxi test; USAF Vanguard contract; Chimera turbine-ramjet engine

name: Alba Orbital
description: Alba Orbital manufactures the world's smallest commercial imaging satellites. Their PocketQube-class 'Unicorn' satellites deliver Earth observation at dramatically lower cost per satellite.
notableAchievements: Unicorn-2 imaging satellite; PocketQube pioneer

name: D-Orbit
description: D-Orbit provides in-space logistics services through its ION Satellite Carrier, a last-mile delivery vehicle that deploys satellites to precise orbital slots from a single rideshare launch. Listed on Euronext with 20+ successful missions.
notableAchievements: 20+ ION missions; Euronext listing; ESA and DoD contracts
activeProducts: ION Satellite Carrier; Aurora satellite bus

name: EnduroSat
description: EnduroSat is a European shared satellite platform provider. The company offers Satellite-as-a-Service, allowing customers to deploy payloads on shared spacecraft without building their own satellite. Raised $26M Series A in 2024.
notableAchievements: Satellite-as-a-Service pioneer; ESA contract awardee; Series A $26M (2024)

name: Latitude (Venture Orbital Systems)
description: Latitude (formerly Venture Orbital Systems) is a French launch startup developing the Zephyr micro-launcher for dedicated small satellite missions from European spaceports. Targeting first launch from Esrange, Sweden.

name: Sidus Space
description: Sidus Space designs, manufactures, and operates multi-sensor satellites for AI-powered Earth observation and space domain awareness. Their LizzieSat platform supports custom payloads for government and commercial customers.
notableAchievements: LizzieSat launched 2024; NASDAQ listed (SIDU); DoD contracts

name: Space Forge
description: Space Forge develops returnable and reusable satellites for in-space manufacturing, producing advanced materials like semiconductors and alloys in microgravity. Their ForgeStar platform is designed for recovery and reuse.
notableAchievements: ForgeStar-1 mission; UK Space Agency funded; In-space manufacturing pioneer

name: HydroSat
description: HydroSat operates thermal infrared Earth observation satellites to monitor water stress, crop health, and wildfire risk. Their data products support precision agriculture and environmental monitoring at high revisit rates.
notableAchievements: Thermal IR constellation; NOAA data buy contract; USDA partnership
activeProducts: Thermal IR satellites; Water stress analytics

name: Starcloud
description: Starcloud is building space-based data centers to provide ultra-low-latency cloud computing from orbit. Backed by Y Combinator, the company aims to leverage the vacuum and cooling advantages of space for high-performance computing workloads including AI inference and edge processing.
notableAchievements: Y Combinator W24 batch; Space data center concept

name: ISPTech
description: ISPTech develops green propulsion systems for small satellites and spacecraft, replacing toxic hydrazine-based thrusters with environmentally friendly alternatives. The German company focuses on high-performance, non-toxic bipropellant engines for LEO and deep-space missions.
notableAchievements: Green propulsion development; ESA technology contracts

name: Skynopy
description: Skynopy operates a distributed ground station network that provides satellite operators with on-demand downlink services across multiple continents. The Paris-based company offers Ground-Station-as-a-Service, reducing the cost and complexity of satellite data reception.
notableAchievements: Multi-continent ground station network; Ground-Station-as-a-Service model

name: Albedo Space
description: Albedo Space operates commercial satellites in Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) at altitudes of 96–300 km, enabling optical imagery at 10 cm resolution — the highest commercially available. Their Clarity-1 satellite launched on SpaceX Transporter-13 in March 2025. VLEO dramatically reduces cost while increasing image sharpness versus traditional LEO constellations.
notableAchievements: Clarity-1 launched March 2025 (first VLEO commercial imager); 10 cm optical resolution — sharpest commercial imagery; ~$100M raised

name: Reditus Space
description: Reditus Space offers Microgravity-as-a-Service (MaaS) through its ENOS platform — reusable satellites that ferry customer payloads to LEO, perform in-space operations in microgravity, and return finished products to Earth. The company removes the ISS bottleneck for pharmaceutical and advanced materials manufacturing in space.
notableAchievements: Y Combinator Winter 2025 batch; $7.6M seed funding; ENOS platform development

name: Reflect Orbital
description: Reflect Orbital builds satellites with large deployable mirrors to redirect sunlight onto Earth's surface after dark, extending effective solar energy production hours and providing responsive illumination for disaster response, agriculture, and remote sites. The technology uses natural sunlight with no active emissions.
notableAchievements: Series A funded 2025; Novel solar illumination satellite concept

name: Lux Aeterna
description: Lux Aeterna is developing Delphi, the world's first fully reusable satellite platform. By separating the satellite bus (mature infrastructure) from rapidly evolving payloads, operators can swap mission payloads between flights, dramatically reducing the cost and timeline of satellite operations.
notableAchievements: Founded by SpaceX/Amazon Kuiper/Loft Orbital veterans; Delphi reusable satellite platform in development

name: The Exploration Company
description: The Exploration Company (TEC) builds Nyx, a reusable cargo spacecraft for resupplying the ISS, future commercial space stations, and lunar Gateway. With ~€230M raised and 300+ employees across Munich and Bordeaux, TEC is Europe's leading commercial cargo vehicle developer, competing alongside US providers for NASA and ESA resupply contracts.
notableAchievements: ~€230M total funding raised; Nyx Earth demonstrator mission; Selected for ESA cargo program; 300+ employees

name: ReOrbit
description: ReOrbit manufactures software-defined satellites and connected spacecraft systems, with a focus on sovereign national security applications. The Helsinki-based company takes a hardware-agnostic approach that allows rapid reconfiguration of satellite missions through software updates, enabling faster response to emerging defense and intelligence requirements.
notableAchievements: Series A funded 2025; Software-defined satellite platform; Defense & national security focus

name: Fleet Space Technologies
description: Fleet Space Technologies operates a proprietary satellite IoT network to power ExoSphere, an AI-driven mineral exploration platform delivering 3D subsurface imaging in real-time with minimal environmental footprint. Clients include major mining companies globally. Fleet raised A$150M in a December 2024 Series D, reaching an ~A$800M valuation — a record for an Australian space startup.
notableAchievements: A$150M Series D (Dec 2024) — record Australian space raise; ~A$800M valuation; ExoSphere mineral exploration platform deployed globally

name: HEO
description: HEO (formerly HEO Robotics) provides space-based space situational awareness through hosted imaging payloads on third-party satellites. The company's sensors image other spacecraft from orbit, giving operators and defence agencies visibility on the health, configuration, and activity of satellites without dedicated inspection vehicles.
notableAchievements: US DoD and Australian Space Agency contracts; Space-based SSA through hosted payloads; Series A funded

name: Neo Space Group
description: Neo Space Group (NSG) is Saudi Arabia's national satellite and space industries champion, established in 2024 and backed by the Public Investment Fund (PIF). NSG is consolidating Saudi Arabia's satellite assets — including stakes in Arabsat and operational ground infrastructure — into a single national entity to accelerate the Kingdom's Vision 2030 space economy goals.
notableAchievements: Backed by Saudi PIF; Consolidating Saudi satellite assets including Arabsat stake; Part of Vision 2030 space economy program

name: Innovian Space
description: Innovian Space is a platform-agnostic space strategy consultancy headquartered in Houston that helps organizations identify and execute economically sustainable uses of space. The firm serves both established space companies and non-space organizations entering the industry, guiding strategy, mission planning, and commercial model development without selling launch access or hardware.
notableAchievements: Houston Space Center Blvd HQ; Platform-agnostic advisory model; Serving established and new-entrant space organizations
activeProducts: Space strategy consulting; Mission planning services

name: Interlune
description: Interlune is developing the technology and systems to extract helium-3 and other natural resources from the Moon for terrestrial markets. Helium-3 — essential for quantum computing, medical imaging, and nuclear fusion research — is vanishingly rare on Earth but abundant in lunar regolith after 4 billion years of solar wind bombardment, commanding ~$20M per kilogram. Founded by Rob Meyerson (ex-Blue Origin President), Gary Lai (ex-Blue Origin Chief Architect), and Apollo 17 astronaut Harrison Schmitt.
notableAchievements: Founded by ex-Blue Origin President Rob Meyerson; Apollo 17 astronaut Harrison Schmitt as co-founder; Helium-3 valued at ~$20M/kg; First company targeting commercial lunar resource extraction
activeProducts: Lunar helium-3 extraction (development); Resource prospecting systems

name: Cowboy Space Corporation (formerly Aetherflux)
description: Formerly known as Aetherflux, the company develops space-based solar power via low-Earth orbit satellite constellations beaming energy via infrared lasers, shifting scope to include orbital data centers and launch systems.
notableAchievements: Raised $275M Series B at a $2B valuation in May 2026; backed by Baiju Bhatt.
activeProducts: Galactic Brain orbital data center; Space solar laser beaming constellation

name: LEAP
description: A dual-use space logistics company focused on point-to-point rocket-powered cargo and payload delivery anywhere on Earth or in orbit within minutes.
notableAchievements: Successfully launched and recovered its Bullfrog suborbital vehicle in May 2026.
activeProducts: Bullfrog launch vehicle; Bighorn orbital logistics vehicle

name: Axelspace
description: Japanese pioneer in microsatellites and commercial Earth observation networks, operating the AxelGlobe constellation.
notableAchievements: Filed for an IPO on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in mid-2026.

name: iQPS (Institute for Q-shu Pioneers of Space)
description: A leading Japanese space startup developing high-resolution, lightweight Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) small satellite constellations.
notableAchievements: Successfully went public on the Tokyo Stock Exchange; launched multiple QPS-SAR satellites.

name: Solestial (York Space Systems)
description: Developer of ultra-thin, radiation-hardened silicon solar cells and blankets designed to power long-endurance space missions.
notableAchievements: Acquired by York Space Systems in May 2026 to enhance end-to-end mission hardware solutions.
